title: Dynamic Worker Runtime Compliance With the Original Research and Post-Grill Plan

tldr.content: Compliant with caveats. The runtime delivers all eight research-mandated changes (S1-S8), all post-grill decisions D1-D10, the six prototype decision conditions, and 9 of 10 original acceptance criteria (AC1-AC5, AC7-AC10 met). Two gaps remain: AC6 periodic re-attestation is implemented but NOT wired into live dispatch (a tier-2 worker is attested once at start), and the research-discovered external trust anchor is deferred (chains default OS-user-bound; final-sink re-auth implemented but un-called live). AGENTS.md is stale-understated; docs overstate 'periodic' and cite an unsupported 'v2.1.154'. Recommend: wire re-attestation and correct docs; otherwise compliant.

executiveSummary.content:
Question: is the dynamic-workers feature now compliant with the original research and the post-grill approach/plan? Four parallel tracks (original research S1-S8; post-grill D1-D10 + plan AC1-AC10; implementation evidence at HEAD 48f84a4; current Anthropic docs) were synthesized, independently challenged, and judged (the first draft failed the judge on factual/citation accuracy and was remediated).

```text
Question -> Triage (DEEP x hybrid)
   -> R1 original research (S1-S8)   -> R2 post-grill + plan (D1-D10, AC1-AC10)
   -> R3 implementation evidence     -> R4 Anthropic docs
   -> Synthesis -> Challenge (downgraded AC6/AC7) -> Judge -> Remediate -> Verified finding
```

Headline: the mechanical core is delivered and wired (scheduler, telemetry/reducer, leases, hooks, tier-1, Docker provider, egress stack + relay + drops, verified-sandbox defaults, decision gate, registry) and 9/10 ACs are met. The material caveats are AC6 (periodic re-attestation unwired) and the deferred external trust anchor, plus documentation drift.

K3. supported — six prototype decision conditions evidenced 1:1 by a regenerated passing artifact [ref-compat-plan][ref-prototype-evidence].
K4. supported — D1-D10 satisfied (D2 tier-2 periodic element = the AC6/K6 gap) [ref-approach][ref-provider].
K5. supported — mediated egress AC7 default-deny + relay + drops + keyed chain [ref-egress][ref-egress-net][ref-runtime].

detailSections.content:
D1 Compliance vs the original research change-set: S1-S8 each have implementation + wired call sites + tests; the mandated child-result contract and worker-event taxonomy (taskId/workerId/invocationId/toolId, lifecycle names) are present. S8 is documentation-only by design [ref-compat-plan][ref-telemetry].

D2 Compliance vs the post-grill plan/approach: D1-D10 satisfied; AC1-AC5 and AC7-AC10 met; AC6 partial (below) [ref-orig-plan][ref-approach].

D3 Decision condition: satisfied — prototype-gate.json records P1-P6 pass (regenerated by the T011 test), and the isolation matrix (7 properties) passes live under Docker [ref-prototype-evidence][ref-decision-evidence].

D4 AC6 periodic re-attestation deviation: createReattestationMonitor is a complete fail-closed monitor with no production caller besides the decision-gate probe; policy.attestation.cadenceMs is never consumed, so post-start drift is undetected on the live path [ref-provider][ref-decision-gate].

D5 Trust-anchor deviation: the research required a keyed/signed head anchored outside the worker trust domain; the delivered keyed chains are external-to-worker but OS-user-bound by default, and authorizeFinalSink/reauthorizeAttestation are not invoked live; host-external custody is deferred per g3-ruling [ref-egress][ref-docs][ref-g3-ruling].

D6 Isolation-gate coverage: at the index seam, a sandbox route is gated only when the adapter reports effectiveIsolation; the in-process adapter and preflight gate can still fire on declared-isolation fallback [ref-index][ref-preflight].

D7 Documentation drift: docs overstate tier-2 'periodic' and cite 'v2.1.154' (unsupported by the current workflows page); AGENTS.md is stale-UNDERstated; g3-ruling.md:24 is stale [ref-docs][ref-agents][ref-g3-ruling][ref-anthropic-workflows].

D8 Anthropic conformance (external): the design aligns with current vendor guidance — definitions as data with documented precedence; read-only-first concurrency; fail-closed sandbox option; worktree isolation; OTel workflow.run_id/agent_id/tool_use_id mapping (treat transcript joins as version-specific) [ref-anthropic-subagents][ref-anthropic-workflows][ref-anthropic-sandboxing][ref-anthropic-monitoring].

recommendation.content:
Recommend: treat the feature as COMPLIANT WITH CAVEATS. It meets the original research (S1-S8), the post-grill decisions (D1-D10), 9 of 10 original acceptance criteria, and the six-condition prototype gate. Confidence: high for the mechanical core; medium for the trust/isolation caveats.

To reach full compliance, close these gaps: (1) wire createReattestationMonitor into the live sandbox runtime and consume policy.attestation.cadenceMs so post-start drift kills a long-lived worker (AC6); (2) either invoke authorizeFinalSink/reauthorizeAttestation on the live terminal path or record OS-user-bound anchoring as the accepted g3-ruling boundary in the acceptance criteria; (3) make the isolation gate refuse a node whose required isolation is unknown regardless of adapter shape; (4) correct docs/AGENTS.md/g3-ruling status text (remove the unsupported v2.1.154 citation).

What would change the answer: if AC6 is read as a hard requirement, the verdict is non-compliant until (1) lands. Cost of being wrong: a long-lived tier-2 worker could drift post-attestation undetected, and a same-OS-user process could forge the audit chain.

unverifiedClaims.content:
U1. Productivity/latency/cost/correctness gains were not measured and must not be inferred (doNotInfer) [ref-compat-plan].
U2. CI evidence freshness: live Docker proofs are CI-skippable and decision-gate.json is rewritten by test runs; the checked-in live artifact was produced on a Docker host [ref-closure-review][ref-decision-evidence].
U3. Anthropic cap values (concurrency 20, depth 3, 16 concurrent / 4096 items / 1000 agents) are version- and plan-dependent policy inputs; re-verify before use [ref-anthropic-subagents][ref-anthropic-workflows].
U4. The isolation-gate adapter-shape condition was inferred from source, not exhaustively exercised on every shipped route.

processAppendix.content: Tier DEEP x hybrid. Tracks: R1 original research; R2 post-grill + plan; R3 implementation evidence at HEAD; R4 current Anthropic docs. Synthesized primary-led; challenger (downgraded AC6/AC7 handling, surfaced AGENTS.md understatement and closure-review/g3 staleness) and judge (failed factual/citation accuracy on draft v1; remediated to v2) were independent; VERIFY primary-personal. Residual: no production telemetry was executed to confirm runtime behavior; conclusions rest on source + tests + recorded artifacts.

claims.statement: Of the original plan's ten acceptance criteria, AC1-AC5 and AC8-AC10 are met; AC7 (egress mediation default-deny, credential-free, chain-valid) is ALSO met — the broker relay landed (egress-broker.mjs:818, wired verified-sandbox-runtime.mjs:262, live test passes); AC6 (tier-2 periodic re-attestation) is NOT met on the live path — createReattestationMonitor is started only by the decision-gate probe (decision-gate.mjs:470) and policy.attestation.cadenceMs is unread. Note: the closure-review artifact wrongly records AC6 as 'met' and its N5/AC7 residual is superseded.

All eight research-mandated change-set items S1-S8 are implemented. S1-S7 are wired into the live path; S8 is satisfied as documentation-only by design (the research acceptance was 'ids align OR documented mapping exists'), not as live runtime correlation.

The six prototype decision conditions are evidenced 1:1 by a passing recorded artifact (prototype-gate.json P1-P6, verdict pass, failedConditions []); the artifact is regenerated by tests/orchestrate-decision-gate.test.mjs (T011) via runPrototypeGate, not hand-authored.

Post-grill decisions D1-D10 are satisfied: full scheduler (D1), two isolation tiers (D2), telemetry /2 (D3), capabilities /2 (D4), fold + rehydration (D5), documented non-blocking id mapping (D6), hybrid validated scheduler (D7), six phases in one plan (D8), dedicated worker entry (D9), thin env-gated child adapter (D10). Caveat: D2's tier-2 'periodic re-attestation' element is the same AC6/K7 gap (attested once at start only).

Mediated egress (AC7) is default-deny with an on-the-wire policy listener, a dual-homed broker, a broker->host relay, real NFLOG per-drop capture fed to a keyed chain, credential injection only on allow, and budget enforcement; a Docker e2e asserts allow-via-listener, default-deny, and a recorded dropped-unmediated dial.

The core planes are implemented and wired: dynamic scheduler with full validation and plan-route refusal; telemetry /2 worker events with reducer/sequence rehydration; per-worker leases/heartbeat in the store; all seven lifecycle hooks; tier-1 hardened worktree (env scrub, descendant kill, worktree validation).

Periodic re-attestation (T015/AC6) is implemented as a fail-closed monitor but is NOT wired into the live dispatch path: createReattestationMonitor is started only by the decision-gate probe, and policy.attestation.cadenceMs is never read; a long-lived tier-2 worker is attested once at start only, so post-start drift is undetected on the live path.

The research's discovered requirement to anchor the keyed/signed head outside the worker trust domain is only partially met: the chains are keyed and external-to-worker but default to OS-user-bound; authorizeFinalSink (egress-broker.mjs:544) and reauthorizeAttestation (docker-worker-provider.mjs) are implemented and tested but NOT invoked on a live terminal path; only host-external acceptance is deferred per the g3-ruling.

At the index dispatch seam, declared verified-sandbox isolation is enforced only when the adapter exposes effectiveIsolation; a custom host/fixture adapter that omits it returns {action:'invoke'} without the gate (index.mjs:485). Scope note: the in-process adapter and preflight isolationGate can still fire on declared-isolation fallback, so this is a seam-specific gap, not a universal one.

AGENTS.md is stale and UNDERstated at HEAD (not overstated): it says tier-2 'is not yet wired into the live dispatch path and the declared execution.isolation/attestation capability is not yet enforced', but the wiring now exists (index.mjs:479-543; driver --verified-sandbox run-orchestrator.mjs:736) and the live test passes.

The closure-review artifact is stale on two points: its AC6 'met' is false (no live re-attestation) and its N5/AC7 residual is superseded (the broker relay is implemented at egress-broker.mjs:818 and live-tested). Its N2 is already marked resolved.

Documentation is partially overstated: docs/dynamic-worker-runtime.md advertises tier-2 'periodic' re-attestation as implemented (it is library-only) and cites an Anthropic 'v2.1.154' workflow requirement that the current workflows page does not contain. The g3-ruling.md line claiming 'final-sink reauthorization (zero code matches)' is also now stale (authorizeFinalSink exists).

The compat-plan six-condition prototype gate is implemented test-locally and regenerated by tests/orchestrate-decision-gate.test.mjs (T011) via runPrototypeGate; the shipped decision-gate.mjs implements a DIFFERENT six conditions (C1-C6) plus the isolation matrix — so 'six conditions' names two different sets that must not be conflated.
Productivity, latency, cost, and correctness gains from the dynamic-worker runtime were not measured; the research explicitly forbids inferring them from Anthropic product behavior.
The live Docker proofs are CI-skippable; the recorded live decision-gate.json was produced on a Docker host and the artifact is rewritten by test runs, so evidence freshness is runner-dependent.
